segments.t: All right, we are going to stay, of course, on anthropic.
But let's kind of talk about that and broaden it out a bit as the markets are down across the board today.
Joining us now is York for Lives co-partner and senior managing director Dan Ives.
Kind of an odd day, Dan.
You've got anthropic, which is still up, but it's well off of its first trade.
So I want to make that clear, sort of two numbers on anthropic.
But yet the macro markets S&P down six days in a row, the whole I stack down again.
What's Dan Ives take on everything that is happening right now?
Yeah, it's a tale of two cities.
I think on one part, anthropic's a watershed event for tech.
I think if you look, the success that you've seen here on the IPO, the appetite, I think you start institutionally in terms of the roadshow.
And this is foundational to the AI build out.
And I think that's just important in terms of this IPO.
I does think it weighs the groundwork for open AI in 2027.
But on the other hand, look, we're going through a dark period for tech.
I think part of it is just in video, the worries about China.
You talk about the AMD short report.
Investors are trying to just figure out where the bottom is here.
And I just I view this.
It's a panic moment, but it's not stopping.
I mean, we're less than 15 percent through the build out of the AI revolution.
Everything anthropic talks about.
That's just the piece of what I view as this foundational bull thesis is not in any way dented despite what we're seeing.
And that's why it's walking investors through this.
I like how you put that, Dan.
And I think the big question everyone wants to know is, are we going to look back and laugh at a two trillion dollar valuation thinking?
How much could that grow?
But then whale rock is stuck in my head.
You know, a firm that's been investing in technology, a hedge fund, Boston based for 15 years.
The guy's best idea is his single biggest pick was anthropic.
He sees us at just the beginning.
